text_blocks.snippet: Ledderhose disease, also known as plantar fibromatosis, is a condition that causes thickening and hardening of the connective tissue (fascia) on the sole of the foot. The main symptoms include:

list.snippet: Hard lumps or nodules: These typically appear on the inner or middle part of the foot, near the arch.
Pain: The lumps can be painful, especially when walking, standing, or putting on shoes.
Stiffness: The thickened fascia can make it difficult to bend or straighten the toes.
Deformity: In severe cases, the lumps can cause the foot to become misshapen.
Toe contractures: In rare cases, the lumps can cause the toes to curl or contract.

text_blocks.snippet: Swelling, Redness, Numbness or tingling, and Difficulty wearing shoes.
It's important to note that Ledderhose disease is usually benign (non-cancerous). However, it can be uncomfortable and affect daily activities.
